songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: Fiery Jerry leads & Pigpen organ power a raw Hollywood Bowl jam
ai_show_review.blurb: The set bursts open with an expansive Viola Lee Blues and rolls through tight renditions of Cold Rain And Snow and Beat It On Down The Line. Jerry’s scorching guitar work and Pigpen’s organ/harmonica fire drive the jams into Alligator and a wild Feedback finale. Despite a crude audience tape, the performance shines.
ai_show_review.review: On September 15, 1967 the Grateful Dead took the Hollywood Bowl by storm, delivering a blistering first set that still excites listeners despite being captured on a low‑fidelity audience recording. Jerry Garcia’s guitar is in full‑hog mode, carving scorching leads through the 13‑minute “Viola Lee Blues” and propelling the band into a ferocious “Alligator”. Ron "Pigpen" McKernan adds that unmistakable 1960s vibe with pounding organ riffs and wailing harmonica, especially on the soulful “Morning Dew”. Phil Lesh’s thumping fretless bass holds down the groove while the rhythm section pushes forward, even as the tape drops out and hiss fills the gaps. The set closes with a chaotic burst of feedback that perfectly captures the era’s experimental spirit.

best_recording.reason: Only available source; despite drop‑outs it captures the raw energy and standout performances of the night.
